btSpeakers.searchingHint: Looking for speakers nearby. This takes about ten seconds.

sources.shareHint: Folders this player publishes on the network, so you can copy music onto it from a computer.
sources.smbAltHostHint: If the player's IP address changes, use the name {host} in place of the address.
sources.smbHowtoIntro: Copy music onto "{name}" from any computer on the same network. The player must be switched on.
sources.smbHowtoWin1: Open File Explorer, click the address bar, type {path} and press Enter.
sources.smbHowtoWin2: When Windows asks for credentials, enter the username and password above and tick "Remember my credentials".
sources.smbHowtoWin3: To keep it handy, right-click the folder and choose "Map network drive…", ticking "Reconnect at sign-in": it will then appear under This PC at every start-up.
sources.smbHowtoMac1: In the Finder choose Go → Connect to Server (⌘K).
sources.smbHowtoMac3: Choose "Registered User", enter the username and password above, and tick "Remember this password in my keychain".
sources.smbHowtoMac4: The folder opens in the Finder and stays under Locations in the sidebar.
sources.smbHowtoMacTip: To mount it automatically at every login, add the mounted volume under System Settings → General → Login Items.
sources.wizIntro: Music kept on a NAS or another computer. The player looks for them on your network; you only have to pick one.

display.changeFailed: Could not change the display mode
display.resolutionHelp: On large screens the interface is drawn at full panel resolution, which keeps the graphics chip busy. Rendering it lower and letting the screen enlarge it makes everything much smoother, at the cost of some sharpness.
display.confirmResolution: The device's interface will close and reopen after a few seconds. Playback is not interrupted. Continue?
display.refreshHelp: Both the screen scaling and the interface's own redraws are tied to the panel's refresh rate, so lowering it reduces graphics-chip load — roughly 40% less on this hardware. Applies immediately, no restart.
display.refreshUnsupported: This device's screen does not offer a lower refresh rate to switch to.
display.confirmRefresh: The device screen will switch to a lower refresh rate. Continue?

display.pointerHelp: Show the mouse pointer on screen, or hide it if you only use the touchscreen. Shown by default, so the on-screen setup wizard stays usable.
display.pointerUnavailable: Pointer control is not available on this device.
display.playerHelp: Turn the player itself off for a server-only unit — Lyrion Music Server and everything else keeps running, this device just never plays audio locally. Useful for a box in a closet driving other players elsewhere.
display.confirmPlayerOff: This device will stop playing audio locally. Lyrion Music Server and remote control keep working. Continue?
display.playerChangeFailed: Could not change the player on/off state
display.engineHelp: Which of the two interfaces runs on the device's screen. The new one (Qt) draws straight on the screen, with no browser: it uses less power and stays smooth even on 4K screens. Music keeps playing when you switch.
display.confirmEngine: The interface on the device's screen will close and come back with the one you picked. Playback continues. Go ahead?

timezone.hint: A fresh install has no way to ask for this, so it defaults to UTC — pick the device's real one here.

updates.keepPowered: The update continues on the device even if you close this page. Just keep it powered on.

companion.hint: Scan the QR code from the Osmium Sound Companion app to pair your phone.

Scan the QR code to download it. Note: DSP, updates, reboot and multiroom role stay manageable only from the device screen and this web interface.
companionIos.open: Open LyrPlay on the App Store
companionIos.disclaimer: LyrPlay is a third-party app, not developed by or affiliated with this project. It is only recommended as a compatible Lyrion/Squeezebox client.

backup.hint: Save the device's configuration, Lyrion preferences and playlists. Set a passphrase to also include credentials (Wi-Fi, SMB shares, this web-admin account) in an encrypted, restorable file — without one, only non-secret settings are saved.
backup.passphraseHint: Leave empty for a plain backup with no credentials. Set one to also save Wi-Fi networks, SMB passwords and this account, encrypted.
backup.restoreConfirm: Restore this backup? A safety copy of the current configuration is taken first.
backup.deleteConfirm: Delete this backup? This cannot be undone.
backup.scheduledHint: Runs unattended, so it never includes credentials — only device settings, sources and Lyrion preferences/playlists.

system.rebootComingBack: Waiting for the device to come back online.
system.rebootAutoReconnect: This page will reconnect automatically — no need to refresh.

system.supportBundleHint: Downloads a zip with device logs and system information, useful for diagnosing an issue remotely.

system.factoryStarted: Factory reset started — the device will restart

debug.bootHint: For a device that hangs at boot or shutdown behind the splash screen instead of failing cleanly — possibly a hidden kernel panic. Both settings need a reboot to take effect.
debug.plymouthHelp: Shows real boot/shutdown text instead of the graphical splash, so a hang or kernel panic is actually visible on the screen.
debug.kdump: Save a memory dump on kernel panic
debug.kdumpHelp: Reserves a small amount of RAM to capture the crash to disk (/var/crash) so it can be inspected after a kernel panic.
debug.kdumpNotInstalled: Installs the crash-dump tools the first time this is turned on (needs Internet access).
debug.rebootRequired: Saved — reboot the device for this to take effect.
debug.rebootPrompt: Reboot the device now to apply this?

netCheck.openHelp: Finds where the connection stops: cable or Wi-Fi, router, internet or the update server.
netCheck.help: Osmium checks, one step at a time, whether it can reach the update server, and tells you where it stops.
netCheck.running: Checking… it takes at most half a minute.
netCheck.failed: The check could not start: the device's service did not answer.

err.noLink: Not connected to any network: check the cable or the Wi-Fi.
err.noAddress: Connected, but it has no address yet.
err.noDhcp: Connected, but the router did not give it an address.
err.weakSignal: Weak Wi-Fi signal: move it closer to the router or use a cable.
err.noGateway: The network did not say which router to use.
err.noPing: The router ignores ping, but it is there and working.
err.packetLoss: Some messages to the router get lost ({loss}%).
err.blockedIps: Direct connections are blocked, but the update server can be reached.
err.dns: Names cannot be looked up: the DNS server does not answer.
err.dnsPartial: Some names cannot be looked up.
err.clockOff: The clock is off by {time}: secure connections may fail.
err.clockWrong: The clock is wrong: secure connections fail.
err.fallback: The main server does not answer, but a backup does: updates still work.
err.rateLimited: GitHub is refusing requests for a while (too many).
err.badManifest: The server answered with something unexpected.
err.tlsCert: Security certificate refused: check the clock.

verdict.ok: All good: the device reaches the update server.
verdict.warn: It works, with a caveat: see the steps in yellow.
verdict.link: The problem is the device's own connection: check the cable or the Wi-Fi.
verdict.router: The problem is between the device and the router: restart the router and check the cable or the Wi-Fi.
verdict.internet: The router answers but does not reach the internet: the problem is the router or your internet provider.
verdict.dns: The internet works but names cannot be looked up: restart the router, or set other DNS servers in the network settings.
verdict.clock: The clock is wrong and secure connections fail: check the time zone and restart the device.
verdict.ota: Your internet works: it is the update server that does not answer right now. Try again later; if it keeps happening, a filter on your network may be blocking it.
verdict.download: The update server answers but the download does not start: try again later, or check for filters on your network.

verdictWarn.link: It works, but the Wi-Fi signal is weak: move the device closer to the router or use a cable.
verdictWarn.router: It works, but the link to the router drops now and then: if the music stops, check the Wi-Fi or the cable.
verdictWarn.internet: It works: your network blocks some connections, but not the ones updates need.
verdictWarn.dns: It works, but some addresses cannot be found: if updates fail, restart the router.
verdictWarn.clock: It works, but the device's clock is a little off: check the time zone.
verdictWarn.ota: It works: the main server does not answer, so the device uses the backup one.
